gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-006 identifies that the claimed global H² regularity and resulting sufficient-condition guidance fail without an appropriate boundary-regularity hypothesis, gives a reentrant-corner counterexample with A=I, and supplies the corresponding boundary-geometry repair. This is the specific defect in the gold applicability claim that A being Lipschitz alone guarantees Assumption I.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both entries identify the omission of boundary geometry or equivalent elliptic regularity from the purported sufficient conditions for the global Dirichlet H² estimate, despite smooth or Lipschitz coefficients, so the applicability claim is false on general bounded Lipschitz domains.

component_coverage.gold_component: The claim that coefficient regularity alone guarantees the global Dirichlet H² estimate and hence Assumption I omits a necessary boundary-regularity condition; reentrant-corner domains provide a counterexample, and the repair is to impose suitable global boundary regularity.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-006 independently diagnoses the missing boundary geometry, demonstrates failure of H² regularity on a reentrant-corner domain even for A=I, notes the resulting false sufficient-condition remark, and proposes a C^{1,1}-type repair. It therefore covers the full substantive gold concern.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-013 concerns hidden time-step dependence in estimates caused by nodal sampling of time-regularity norms. It does not identify the distinct defect that Example 1 gives mutually inconsistent declarations of the numerical time step, nor does it establish which value was used or require correcting the declarations. The common reference to Δt is only a shared topic.
